title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from p.310). E is a once-punctured torus (an elliptic curve E), with fundamental group π' of type Π_{1,1}. ₂E is its 2-torsion (4 points). The space E∖₂E has fundamental group π̃' of type (1,4), with I(π̃') of cardinal 4. The group G = Z/2 = {±1} acts on it by the inversion x ↦ −x. This action is free on E∖₂E and fixes each 2-torsion point, so G acts trivially on I(π̃'). Filling the three holes J = I∖{i₀} recovers π' (eq. 59).

This page.
- The extension 1 → π̃' → Σ̃ → Z/2 → 1 (eq. 60) is the mixed fundamental group of (E∖₂E, G).
- Since the action is free, Σ̃ is the ordinary fundamental group of the quotient V = (E∖₂E)/{±1} (eq. 61). V is the sphere minus the 4 branch values of the Weierstrass/Legendre double cover, a surface of type (0,4).
- So Σ̃ carries a natural 'loop-group' structure of type (0,4), induced from that of π̃'.
- Its set of punctures is I(Σ̃) ≅ I(π̃')/G ≅ I(π̃') (eq. 62), since G acts trivially on the punctures.
- The distinguished puncture i₀ (the image of the origin) lets one 'fill the hole at i₀'. This gives an effective loop group of type (0,3), written π = L(π') (eq. 63). This defines a functor L from (1,1)-loop groups to (0,3)-loop groups.

Converse direction (started here, continued p.311).
- Start from π of type (0,3). Pass to a (0,4)-group π̃ with a marked i₀, so that I(π̃) = {i₀} ⊔ I(π).
- Take the kernel of the canonical map π̃ → Z/2. This map is the 'sum of coefficients' on (π̃_ab)₂ ≅ (Z/2)^{I}, i.e. nontrivial on every puncture loop. The kernel is a group of type (1,4).
- Fill three holes to get back a (1,1)-group.

This is the group-theoretic, 'loop-equation' version of the classical Legendre correspondence between M_{1,1} (with level-2 structure) and M_{0,4} / P¹∖{0,1,∞}. It serves Grothendieck's programme of describing the Teichmüller tower at levels (0,3), (0,4), (1,1) by purely algebraic 'groupes à lacets' and their equations.
errors: Eq. (62): the transcription's final term I(π') would be wrong, since I(π') has cardinal 1. In the image the last term is I(π̃'), which is consistent because G acts trivially on I(π̃'). No mathematical error then.
The notation drifts: the extension is called ξ̃ on p.310 and Σ̃ here. This is harmless.

ideas.what: π₁ of the punctured elliptic curve minus its 2-torsion, modulo the inversion, is π₁ of a 4-punctured sphere. Filling the origin's image gives a (0,3) group, so there is a functor L: (1,1)-loop groups → (0,3)-loop groups, together with its inverse construction via the canonical 'sum of coefficients' double cover.
ideas.modern_name: Legendre / Weierstrass double cover relating Γ_{1,1} and Γ_{0,4}; the passage between the profinite fundamental groups of E∖0 and of P¹∖{0,1,∞} used in elliptic Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Fricke). In the GT context: Nakamura, and Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997), among others
ideas.where_published: The low-modular-dimension levels (0,3), (0,4), (1,1), (1,2) are discussed in Esquisse d'un programme. This specific loop-group formulation appears only in the Longue Marche manuscripts.

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'groupe à lacets' structure: puncture set I(π), orientation module T, the effective notion, and 'bouchage des trous' (filling punctures), transported along finite étale quotients
ideas.modern_name: Peripheral structure / inertia classes of surface groups; forgetful (filling) maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in the study of mapping class groups and anabelian geometry
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (manuscript)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful algebraic transcription of the classical (1,1) ↔ (0,4)/(0,3) correspondence via the inversion double cover. It is well known topologically and used throughout the GT literature. Only the 'groupes à lacets' formalism is idiosyncratic.
transcription_corrections: Eq. (62): the last term is I(π̃') (with tilde), not I(π').
'(61)' labels V=(E∖₂E)/{±1}; the line above it reads 'groupe fondamental de'.
On the bottom line the word 'effectif' is crossed out and replaced by 'à lacets', consistent with the transcription.
